evidence_class: independent observation (the Independent observation class of docs/acceptance-evidence-policy.md): read-only gh REST GET calls on 2026-10-03 over GitHub's own Actions run, job and step records and the full-suite log artifacts of this public repository (platform records), the 1,025-SHA pairing, which the input records as cross-checked on two endpoints (the second endpoint was not recorded: queries), and the pull_request conclusion counts for 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-02 recomputed independently with identical cells (an independent run-level pairing of those two days differs from the measuring agent's by one macOS-only failure and is not reconciled: see limitations). What was kept is a compiled summary of those observations (source.published_input), not their returned payloads or per-call argument vectors (queries.not_retained). Later observations on 2026-10-03, with exact argument vectors, times, exit codes and payload hashes (source.later_reads), back the corrections listed in source.changes_from_input. Not an upstream test, not a local integration check and not acceptance of any change
kind_basis: artifact_measurement as in evidence/receipts/claude-spend-attribution-20260929.json, a count-only measurement of native records; docs/evidence.md defines the kind for tokenizer counts of a public artifact pair, and unlike such a pair these counts cannot be recounted after retention (limitations)
claim: Read-only gh REST GET calls on 2026-10-03 over this public repository's GitHub Actions records for runs created 2026-09-25 to 2026-10-02 UTC (8,782 runs; every query partition under the 1,000-result cap; the duration samples are the newest runs at measurement time, created on 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-03) measured: both required test jobs run the whole suite serially in one process (Linux validate 1,727-1,745 s on sampled pull_request runs and 1,167-1,828 s on push runs against a 2,400 s limit; macOS validate-macos 1,932-2,394 s, median 2,154 s over 12 pull_request runs, against 3,600 s, its full-suite step 84% of the median job); the serial macOS suite grew from 5,596 tests in 489 s (2026-09-25) to 9,483 tests in 1,830 s (2026-10-02), 9,750 the latest seen; pull_request runs of Validate published evidence were 1,354 (816 success, 88 failure, 449 cancelled, 1 action_required) and of Adoption bootstrap smoke 1,028 (700, 75, 252, 1); 672 of all 712 cancelled runs in the window (94.4%; 701 of them pull_request runs of these two workflows) were superseded by a newer run of the same workflow, branch and event; and of 1,025 pull_request head SHAs paired across the Linux and macOS runs, 695 passed both, 46 failed both, 30 failed only on macOS (2.9% of SHAs, 3.9% of the 779 decisive pairs), 8 failed only on Linux and 246 were incomplete.
limitations: Counts are run-level unless stated; a re-run overwrites a run's conclusion.
Timeouts among the 712 cancelled runs were not classified; 40 cancelled runs have no superseding run.
The by-prefix artifact table covers 97% of artifacts.
Linux sample runs for supply-chain and action-compatibility date from 2026-09-22 to 09-26 (no later success runs).
Evidence class: measured via gh read-only on 2026-10-03 (platform records, independent observation), not an upstream test.

Retention: GitHub's retention policy covers checks, workflow runs and commit statuses from 2026-10-01 (90 days by default, 1 to 90 days for a public repository; this repository's artifact and log retention setting read 90 days on 2026-10-03, source.later_reads), and the full-suite log artifacts named in data keep 30 days. The run ids in data are pointers that stop resolving then. The measurement kept neither its returned payloads nor its per-call argument vectors (queries.not_retained), so its counts can be re-derived from GitHub only while those records exist; after that this receipt and its published input are a recorded summary that can be quoted but not re-checked, and for the measurement they do not meet docs/acceptance-evidence-policy.md lines 57-60 (exact argument vectors, times and returned output).

Independent pairing difference: an independent run-level pairing of 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-02 found 4 macOS-only failures among 140 decisive pairs, while data.macos_unique_failures.per_day_both_passed_both_failed_macos_only_linux_only_incomplete (the measuring agent's pairing) gives 5 among 143 decisive pairs (218 paired heads in all; 3 on 2026-10-01, 2 on 2026-10-02). The difference is not reconciled; a likely cause is run-level against job-level pairing or list completeness, which is an inference.

Test names for macOS-only failures were read for 17 of the 30 head SHAs (15 by the measuring agent, 2 by the coordinator); the other 13 were not itemized. The input's key failing_tests_for_15_of_the_30 and its limits string (16 runs covering 15 head SHAs plus one duplicate case, 15 not itemized) miscount its own 17-entry list, which covers 17 distinct head SHAs; both are corrected under data.macos_unique_failures (source.changes_from_input). head_sha (12 characters) was added to each entry on 2026-10-03, while the runs still resolved, so identity survives run-id expiry.
The 146 head SHAs whose Linux and macOS runs were both cancelled were not examined at job level.
Whether a macOS-only failure is a real Darwin defect or a flake cannot be read from step names; the proxies are re-runs and later same-SHA successes, and a re-run overwrites a run's conclusion.

The 8-day window applies to the counts. The duration samples (12 macOS and 3 Linux pull-request runs) are the newest runs at measurement time, created on 2026-10-02 and 2026-10-03 (up to 2026-10-03T01:18Z for the macOS sample). The Linux sample's creation range is inferred from run ids above the macOS sample's last id. The push and pull_request duration samples of data.push_versus_pull_request_duplication are the first three successful runs per event at measurement time.

Of the 712 cancelled runs, 701 are pull-request runs of the two workflows in data.pull_request_runs. The other 11 are 8 runs of other workflows and 3 runs of those two workflows on other events (Validate push 1 and workflow_dispatch 1, Adoption workflow_dispatch 1), by a GET listing of all 712 cancelled runs on 2026-10-03 (data.cancelled_run_supersession.other_workflows.composition); the input said all 11 belonged to other workflows.

Failure anatomy coverage: the measurement input did not record which failed runs its anatomy classified. Validate: 80 of its 88 failed pull-request runs. A later reclassification of all 88 on 2026-10-03 (its rule and results in data.failure_anatomy_non_cancelled.coverage) gives 94 failing job instances, 21 of them sota-sources, against the recorded 86 and 13 with every other by_step count equal (policy_gate, which counts sota-sources, rises by the same 8), so the 8 runs left out hold 94 - 86 = 8 instances, 21 - 13 = 8 of them sota-sources: each of the 8 failed only in sota-sources. Over all 88 runs sota-sources therefore has 21 of 94 failing job instances (13 of 86 in the 80) and every other by_step count is unchanged, whichever 8 were left out. Which 8 they were is not established (data.failure_anatomy_non_cancelled.coverage.validate.selection): leaving out any 8 of the 19 runs that failed only in sota-sources reproduces the same counts. Adoption: all 75 failed pull-request runs. Other workflows: 10 of 76 failures (security-scan 7 of 71, dependency-review 2 of 4, native-token-e2e 1 of 1); the other 66 were classified neither by the measurement nor later.

Cache counts: the measurement recorded 130 active caches but 131 by key prefix (130 codeql-overlay-base-database plus 1 macos-embed-model), and its byte total equals the by-prefix sum to 0.1 MiB, which does not indicate which count is right (data.caches_and_artifacts.caches.bytes_reconciliation). Neither the endpoints nor the capture times were recorded, and the difference is not reconciled (data.caches_and_artifacts.caches.count_reconciliation). Two later paired reads on 2026-10-03 showed the same one-cache gap between the usage endpoint's count and the cache listing, with identical byte totals, so snapshot skew is an unlikely explanation for those later pairs; the cause is unknown.

scope: Public-repository CI measurements only; no dollar or allowance figures and no private-repository data (billed minutes of this public repository, which are free, appear only as per-job rounded counts). queries.status: Request forms reconstructed on 2026-10-03, after the measurement, from the coordinator's unpublished measurement plan (its provenance appendix) and the data below. They are templates, not a transcript of the roughly 587 calls. {owner}/{repo} is seathatflowsinourveins/native-agent-stack; <...> marks a value that varied per call, and each form's basis says what it rests on. The gh api forms of the measuring agent's reads, including the reads it shares with the coordinator, give the path only (gh api <path>) because their client flags were not retained. The input records the calls as read-only GETs (data.measured_by); a GH_DEBUG=api check on 2026-10-03 with gh 2.102.0 (not retained) showed that gh run list sends GET requests (actions/workflows, then actions/workflows/<id>/runs).
queries.not_retained: The returned payloads and the per-call argument vectors, times and exit codes of the measuring agent's roughly 587 calls and of the coordinator's recomputation. The receipt is therefore a recorded summary of observations that can be re-derived from GitHub only while its records exist (up to 90 days under GitHub's retention policy, and this repository's retention setting reads 90 days; the full-suite log artifacts keep 30 days), and for the measurement it does not meet docs/acceptance-evidence-policy.md lines 57-60 (exact argument vectors, start and end times, returned output). The later reads in source.later_reads keep their exact argument vectors, times, exit codes and payload hashes; their payloads are withheld.

validate.classification_rule: A failing job instance is a job of the run's latest attempt (GET repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/<run_id>/jobs?filter=latest&per_page=100) whose conclusion is failure, attributed to its first step whose conclusion is failure. The validate job's steps map to the by_step labels by name ('Test validation failure modes', which runs python3 -m unittest, is the unittest step); the sota-sources, verdict-review-gate and secret-scan jobs count as policy_gate and every other instance as real_test_or_gate. The full mapping, the per-run rows and each call are in source.later_reads.

coverage.effect_on_reductions: R3 and R5 of the decision record use the Validate and validate-macos counts, and neither depends on which 8 Validate runs were left out: each of them failed only in sota-sources (validate.selection), so including them raises sota-sources from 13 of 86 to 21 of 94 instances and leaves the unittest step (47) and the validator and lint steps (18) unchanged; R3's basis grows and R5's ordering, in which the test steps dominate, holds. If the 8 are the runs that a later same-SHA run turned green (validate.runs_with_a_later_success), as the input's tally is consistent with, they also fit R3's mechanism (a description edit fixes the gate and starts a new run on the same SHA; the runs API does not expose the action type, so that link is an inference). The 66 unclassified other-workflow failures are outside both counts; whether R5's pre-push check would reach any of them is unknown.
